item.title: Ninety Days on Our Own: Fortress America and the Field Day Mindset
item.description: A few nights before our weekly ragchew, a good friend of mine sent me an email. He’s an Army veteran who spent years around military aviation, so when he talks about the military, I listen. He’d read a story about something the Pentagon is calling FORTRESS America, and he planned to bring it up on the net. He was blunt about his gut reaction: this is not good. Fifty years ago, he wrote, he was way down the chain of command, but even then he knew the military doesn’t train for something just for the fun of it.

item.title: MeshCore Room Servers: Store-and-Forward Messaging Infrastructure
item.description:
Building communication systems is interesting because it’s not just about moving messages from point A to point B. The real challenge is ensuring messages actually arrive when people need them to receive them.

That’s what MeshCore room servers solve.

The Problem They Address

Traditional mesh networks (and many first-generation implementations) work great when everyone’s actively monitoring. Messages fly across the network in real-time. People respond immediately. It’s dynamic and responsive.
